answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on work, whether mapping a lagoon, sourcing ivory substitutes, or surveying karst. The bond stays locked even if the identity quits, so one deposit cannot be recycled through fresh accounts. An attacker fielding 1,000 simultaneous fake sellers must immobilize $100,000; creating more names does not create more bidding capacity without more capital.
